ing: fresh firm white fish (mahi-mahi or snapper)
very fresh, sushi-grade, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
st: Use only very fresh fish from a trusted seller, since it is eaten uncooked in lime juice. Pat the cubes dry and place in a glass bowl.
Pour the lime juice over the fish so every piece is covered and sprinkle with the salt.
Cover and refrigerate for 30 to 40 minutes, stirring once, until the fish turns opaque and white throughout.
Drain off about half of the lime juice.
Stir in the onion, tomato, cucumber and chili.
Pour in [[0.75 cup]] chilled coconut milk and fold gently.
Taste and add more salt or lime juice if needed, then add the cilantro.
Serve cold in bowls or coconut shells within an hour.

ing: large package; foil is a fine swap
st: Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). This home version stands in for the traditional earth oven.
Mix the salt and garlic and rub them onto the pork, chicken and fish.
Soften banana leaves over a flame for 30 seconds, or tear large sheets of foil.
Wrap the pork in a leaf or foil package with a splash of coconut milk and seal tightly. Make a second package for the chicken and a third for the fish.
Wrap the taro and cassava in a fourth package with the rest of the coconut milk.
Put the pork, chicken and root packages on a tray and bake 90 minutes.
Add the fish package and bake another 25 minutes. Pork should reach 145°F (63°C), chicken 165°F (74°C), and the roots should be fork-tender.
Rest the packages 10 minutes, unwrap carefully and serve everything together on a platter.

ing: or fresh spinach and 4 oz kale if unavailable
st: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Wash the leaves well and remove thick stems.
If using taro leaves, boil them in water for 5 minutes until soft, then drain well.
Mix [[0.5 cup]] coconut milk with the onion, garlic, salt, pepper and corned beef if using.
Layer 3 to 4 leaves flat on foil and spoon some of the onion mixture into the center.
Fold the leaves over the filling to make a tight parcel, then wrap in foil.
Repeat to make 6 parcels. Pour [[0.25 cup]] of coconut milk into each foil wrap before sealing.
Place on a tray and bake for 40 minutes until very tender.
Unwrap and serve warm with boiled cassava or taro.

ing: or fresh spinach as a swap
st: Wash the leaves and trim off any tough stems.
Boil the leaves in water for 10 minutes. This removes the itchiness of raw taro, so do not skip it.
Drain and squeeze out the water, then chop roughly.
In a pot, combine [[1 cup]] water, the onion, garlic and chili.
Bring to a simmer and cook 5 minutes.
Add the leaves and [[1.5 cups]] coconut milk.
Simmer gently for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until creamy and very soft.
Season with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and serve with rice or cassava.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and cook the onions for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in [[3 tbsp]] curry powder and a splash of water and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and cook 5 minutes until they break down.
Add the chicken and [[1.5 tsp]] salt and stir to coat. Cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in [[2 cups]] water and add the potatoes. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook for 30 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Uncover, simmer 5 more minutes to thicken, stir in the cilantro, and serve with roti or rice.
Mix the flour and salt in a large bowl.
Add [[1 tbsp]] oil and [[1 cup]] warm water, then stir to form a shaggy dough.
Knead on a floured counter for 8 minutes until soft and smooth.
Cover and rest 30 minutes.
Divide into 8 balls and roll each into a thin round about 8 inches wide.
Brush each lightly with oil.
Cook in a hot dry skillet for about 1 minute per side until puffed with brown spots.
Brush with ghee and stack in a towel to keep soft.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 9 by 13 inch baking dish.
Squeeze the grated cassava in a clean towel to remove extra moisture.
Whisk the eggs, sugar, melted butter, vanilla and salt in a large bowl.
Stir in the coconut milk and condensed milk.
Fold in the cassava until evenly mixed.
Pour into the dish and smooth the top.
Bake for 60 to 70 minutes until the top is deep golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool for at least 30 minutes before slicing, since it firms up as it cools.

ing: muslin cloth or fine strainer bag
st: Put the powdered kava in a muslin cloth or fine strainer bag and tie it closed.
Pour [[2 cups]] of the warm water into a large clean bowl.
Submerge the bag in the water and knead and squeeze it for 5 minutes until the water turns muddy brown.
Add the remaining [[2 cups]] water and keep kneading for 5 more minutes.
Squeeze the bag firmly to push out the last liquid, then discard the pulp.
Serve the drink in small bowls or cups. Offer it in small amounts since it numbs the lips and tongue and is mildly sedating.

ing: or foil to line the dish
st: Heat the oven to 350°F. Line a 9 by 9 inch baking dish with banana leaves, softened over a flame or in hot water, or with foil.
Squeeze the grated cassava in a clean towel to remove extra liquid. Raw cassava must be fully cooked, so it needs the whole baking time.
Mix the cassava, [[0.5 cup]] brown sugar, [[0.5 cup]] grated coconut, [[1 tsp]] vanilla and salt in a bowl.
Stir in [[1 cup]] of the coconut cream until a thick, wet mixture forms. Spread it evenly in the dish.
Cover with foil and bake 50 minutes until the cassava turns translucent and the pudding is firm in the middle.
Uncover, pour the remaining [[0.5 cup]] coconut cream over, and bake 15 minutes more until the top is golden. Cool 15 minutes before cutting.
nt: Baked at 350°F, traditionally steamed in an earth oven
Best swap: thawed frozen grated cassava in place of fresh, same weight, and skip the banana leaves if you have none.
